## Body heating, top cooling and bottom heating (`body-heat`, `top-cool`, `bot-heat`) {#sec-ch09-heating}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** `body-heat` heats every interior cell whose pressure lies in a band at a fixed rate of
temperature change at constant volume; `top-cool` and `bot-heat` remove or add a fixed energy flux, spread evenly
over the top or bottom `depth` cells.
**Switch.** `forcing/body-heat: {dTdt, pmin, pmax}`, defaults 0, 0, 1 [K s$^{-1}$, Pa, Pa];
`top-cool: {flux, depth}`, `flux` $\le0$, default 0 and 1; `bot-heat: {flux, depth}`, `flux` $\ge0$, default 0
and 1 [W m$^{-2}$, cells]. Each off unless its key is present.
**Order.** Exact sources; explicit, first order in time per stage.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch09-heating-body and @eq-ch09-heating-flux.
:::

These three modules are prescribed heat sources for idealised convection. They touch only the total energy, so
they change the temperature and, through it, the pressure; mass and momentum are untouched. `body-heat` is a
volumetric rate; `top-cool` and `bot-heat` stand for a radiative or surface flux at the top or bottom of the
domain, applied only by the block that owns that physical $x_1$ boundary.

The default `pmax` is 1 Pa: a `body-heat` block that does not set `pmin` and `pmax` heats only cells with
$0\le p\le1$ Pa, which in most decks is none.

### Derivation

*Body heating.* At constant volume the internal energy changes by $\rho c_v\,\mathrm{d}T$, so a heating rate
$\dot T$ adds, in one stage and in every interior cell with $p_{\min}\le p_i\le p_{\max}$,

$$
\Delta E_i = \Delta t\,\dot T\,\rho_ic_{v,i} ,
$$ {#eq-ch09-heating-body}

with $c_v$ the mixture value of the equation of state at the cell's state, in `BodyHeatImpl::forward`
([`body_heat.cpp:43-55`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/body_heat.cpp#L43-L55)). For a
constant $c_v$ at fixed density this raises $T$ by exactly $\dot T\Delta t$ [check
`src/snapy_report/ch09/heating_check.py`, output `heating_check.out`, `[C3]`]; a $c_v$ that depends on $T$ makes
it first order in $\Delta t$.

*Boundary fluxes.* A flux $F$ [W m$^{-2}$] spread over the $d$ cells next to the boundary is applied to each of
those cells as a uniform volumetric rate

$$
\Delta E_i = \Delta t\,\frac{F}{h_{\mathrm b}\,d} ,
$$ {#eq-ch09-heating-flux}

with $h_{\mathrm b}$ the width of the boundary cell, `dz`, in `TopCoolImpl::forward`
([`top_cool.cpp:42-56`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/top_cool.cpp#L42-L56)) and `BotHeatImpl::forward` ([`bot_heat.cpp:42-56`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp#L42-L56)). The energy delivered to a column of unit horizontal area is
$\sum_i\Delta E_ih_i = \Delta t\,F\,\bar h/h_{\mathrm b}$, with $\bar h$ the mean width of the $d$ cells: exactly $F$
on uniform cells (`[C1]`), and $F$ times $\bar h/h_{\mathrm b}$ otherwise, 0.872 for cells growing upward by 10 % with
$d=4$ (`[C2]`). On a spherical-polar grid the cell volume is not $h$ times a fixed area, so the delivered power is
not $F$ either; not measured.

*Exact and truncated.* Both sources are exact pointwise for the stage-entry state; nothing is truncated in space.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-heating-column shows where each module acts.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-heating-column
#| fig-cap: "Where the three heating modules act in an $x_1$ column bounded by walls (thick black lines). Blue: the top $d$ cells cooled by top-cool, a flux $F\\le0$ in $\\mathrm{W\\,m^{-2}}$; vermillion: the bottom $d$ cells heated by bot-heat, $F\\ge0$; orange: the cells inside the pressure band $p_{\\min}\\le p\\le p_{\\max}$ (in $\\mathrm{Pa}$) of body-heat; light blue: untouched cells."
#| fig-alt: "A vertical stack of ten cells with the top three, the bottom two and three middle cells shaded, each labelled with the module and its formula."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.fig_heating_column import make_fig
make_fig()
```

All three are cell sources: no stencil and no ghosts are read. `body-heat` acts on interior cells only.
`top-cool` and `bot-heat` slice only in $x_1$, so they also write the $x_2$, $x_3$ ghost cells of their rows, which
the boundary fill overwrites. They run in every stage, explicit, in the forcing loop (@sec-ch09-framework).

### Limits

1. **Stretched cells.** @eq-ch09-heating-flux uses the boundary cell's width for all $d$ cells, so the delivered
   power is $F$ only on uniform cells (`[C2]`).
2. **Curved grids.** No correction for the cell volume of spherical-polar or cubed-sphere grids; not measured.
3. **`depth` larger than the block** is not checked against the block's $x_1$ cells; not tested.
4. **`body-heat` default band** `pmax` = 1 Pa (above).
5. **Under an $x_1$ split** only the block that owns the boundary applies `top-cool` or `bot-heat`; a `depth` that
   reaches into the next block is truncated there. Not tested.
